messages.subject: add unseen animals to capthist
parts:
Hello, I am new to secr and running mark-resight models.  I have multiple sessions where some animals are marked and seen on camera, some animals are marked and not seen on camera, and some animals seen on camera are not marked.  The marking process takes place outside of the camera session and is opportunistic hunter trapping-so would be difficult to model.

So I have managed to get secr to run multisession data for sessions where I have marked animals that are seen.  BUT when I try to include include a session where there were no marked animals seen on camera like this........

Session Animal Occasion Trap
S2         NONE        0               0  

I get an error regarding missing or duplicated animal names and no live releases for S2. Even if I put the phrase nocapt="NONE" in the call to read.capthist
Ideally I would like to get the known marked animals in caphist even if they were not captured because I do have telemetry data on these animals that I would like to use to estimate sigma.  

I have tried the following to no avail, I get errors that the trap location doesn't match anything in the trap file - which it doesn't of course.  But I'm not sure how to format these guys that I know were marked and in the area but were never seen.

S3  ABC   0    0 
S3  XYZ  0   0  

Thanks,

Robin

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: add unseen animals to capthist
parts:
Robin
I personally have two problems with this
1. Mark-resight analyses tend to be flimsy and unconvincing because of errors in recording marks and mark status, doubtful independence of repeat sightings etc. The problems are magnified when you can't model the marking process, as the spatial distribution of marked animals is then pretty much a guess. The problems are not solved by bringing in telemetry data: this may or may not be representative, and with rare exceptions helps only to pin down the sigma parameter. Spatial mark-resight may work with careful design and large samples, but both are rare. This is my personal take, and you didn't ask for that, but it explains why I limit my support: it's up to others who are more enthusiastic to weigh in.
2. I can't put my finger on your data issue. It is possible that 'secr' does not handle multi-session mark-resight analyses with no marked animals in some sessions - I would have to check. That would be easier if we had a minimal example, including a dataset and R code. Can you provide (offline if necessary)?
Murray
